title: A role-gated UI slot renders per the authorisation adapter's decision
asA: operator viewing a page that carries UI elements gated by verb
iWant: elements I am allowed to see to render and elements I am not allowed to see to be absent from the DOM
soThat: the UI does not mislead me about what I can do, and does not tempt exploit attempts by revealing forbidden verbs behind disabled buttons

acceptanceCriteria.description: A UI slot wired to a project verb through the adapter's `can` decision is present in the rendered DOM when `can` returns `true` for the current principal and absent when `can` returns `false`.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a page carrying a UI slot gated on the verb `article.delete`, and a principal for whom `can(principal, 'article.delete')` returns `true`
acceptanceCriteria.when: a page-render probe fetches the page as the signed-in operator and inspects the rendered DOM
acceptanceCriteria.then: the DOM contains the slot's rendered element; a subsequent render as a signed-in operator whose principal returns `false` for the same verb produces a DOM in which the slot is absent (no hidden node, no disabled control, no aria-hidden variant)

acceptanceCriteria.description: The UI slot's absence is not the only defence; the corresponding server-side handler also refuses via `assert` on the same verb when the caller lacks it.
acceptanceCriteria.given: the same page and verb from AC-9106-1, and a principal whose `can` returns `false`
acceptanceCriteria.when: a request bypassing the UI (direct API call) attempts the verb's underlying action
acceptanceCriteria.then: the server-side handler's `assert(principal, 'article.delete')` throws `AUTHZ_FORBIDDEN`; the response status is 403 and no state mutation occurs
